<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is a great King * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Tobíæ
<r>Tob 6:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Proféctus est autem Tobías, et canis secútus est eum, et mansit prima mansióne juxta flúvium Tigris.
<n>2</n> Et exívit ut laváret pedes suos, et ecce piscis immánis exívit ad devorándum eum.
<n>3</n> Quem expavéscens Tobías clamávit voce magna, dicens: Dómine, invádit me.
<n>4</n> Et dixit ei ángelus: Apprehénde bránchiam ejus, et trahe eum ad te.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Peto, Dómine, ut de vínculo impropérii hujus absólvas me, aut certe désuper terram erípias me: ne reminiscáris delícta mea vel paréntum meórum, neque vindíctam sumas de peccátis meis:
* Quia éruis sustinéntes te, Dómine.
<r>℣.</r> Omnia enim judícia tua justa sunt, et omnes viæ tuæ misericórdia et véritas: et nunc, Dómine, meménto mei.
<r>℟.</r> Quia éruis sustinéntes te, Dómine.

b.1f3eec51a6:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>O</c>ctávo Kaléndas Octóbris Luna vicésima tértia. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>F</h>estum beátæ Maríæ Vírginis de Mercéde nuncupátæ, Ordinis redemptiónis captivórum sub ejus nómine Institutrícis, de cujus Apparitióne ágitur quarto Idus Augústi.
<h>B</h>ríxiæ deposítio sancti Anathalónis Epíscopi, qui, beáti Bárnabæ Apóstoli discípulus, in ejus locum Epíscopus Ecclésiæ Mediolanénsis succéssit.
<h>I</h>n Pannónia sancti Gerárdi, Epíscopi Morisénæ sedis et Mártyris, Hungarórum Apóstoli nuncupáti, patrícii Véneti; qui, cum e Chanadiénsi óppido Albam Regálem se conférret, prope flumen Danúbium ab infidélibus impetítus, lapídibus óbrutus ac tandem láncea transfíxus occúbuit, sicque primus pátriam nóbili martýrio illustrávit.
<h>A</h>ugustodúni natális sanctórum Mártyrum Andóchii Presbýteri, Thyrsi Diáconi, et Felícis. Hi, a beáto Polycárpo, Smyrnénsi Epíscopo, ab Oriénte dirécti ad docéndam Gálliam, ibídem flagéllis duríssime cæsi, ac tota die invérsis mánibus suspénsi, et in ignem missi sunt, sed non combústi; tandem eórum colla véctibus feriúntur, et ita Mártyres gloriosíssime coronántur.
<h>I</h>n Ægýpto pássio sanctórum Paphnútii et Sociórum Mártyrum. Ipse, vitam in solitúdine agens, cum audíret multos Christiános in vínculis retinéri, sponte, divíno Spíritu cóncitus, Præfécto se offert, et Christiánam religiónem líbere profitétur; a quo primum caténis férreis costríngitur, et in equúleo diutíssime torquétur, deínde cum áliis plúrimis ad Diocletiánum míttitur, cujus jussu, ipse palmæ affígitur, céteri autem ferro necántur.
<h>C</h>halcedóne sanctórum quadragínta novem Mártyrum, qui post martýrium sanctæ Euphémiæ, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, damnáti ad béstias, et, cum ab iis divínitus líberi evasíssent, demum, gládio percússi, migravérunt in cælum.
<h>A</h>rvérnis, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Rústici, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>F</h>lavíaci, in território Bellovacénsi, sancti Geremári, Presbýteri et Abbátis.
<h>S</h>eptémpedæ, in Picéno, deposítio sancti Pacífici, Sacerdótis ex Ordine Minórum et Confessóris, exímiæ patiéntiæ viri et solitúdinis amóre præclári, quem Gregórius Papa Décimus sextus in Sanctórum cánonem rétulit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.3de825d77f:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>S</c>eptember 24th 2027, the 23rd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>O</h>n the same day, holy Anathalon; he was a disciple of the blessed Apostle Barnabas, and followed after him as Bishop of the Church of Milan.
<h>I</h>n Hungary, (in the year 1047,) the holy martyr Gerard (Sagredo,) Bishop of Chonad, called the Apostle of Hungary. By birth he was a nobleman of Venice, and was the first of his countrymen who adorned their fatherland by the glory of martyrdom.
<h>A</h>t Autun, the holy martyrs Andochius a Priest, Thyrsus a Deacon, and Felix. Blessed Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna, sent Andochius and Thyrsus from the east to teach in Gaul, where they were (received as guests by the noble Felix. In the end they and he were) most heavily scourged, and hung up all day by the hands, then cast into the fire, but as they were not burnt their necks were broken with bars, and so they received a right glorious crown.
<h>I</h>n Egypt, (in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian,) the holy martyrs Paphnutius and his Companions.
<h>H</h>e was dwelling in the desert when he heard that many Christians were kept in chains wherefore the Spirit of God moved him to go of his own free will to the Prefect, and profess himself a Christian. The Prefect had him first bound in iron fetters, and racked for a very long time then he sent him, and many others, to Diocletian, by whose command Paphnutius was hung upon a palm-tree, and the others were beheaded.
<h>A</h>t Chalcedon, forty-nine holy martyrs, who were condemned to be devoured by wild beasts, under the Emperor Diocletian, after the martyrdom of holy Euphemia, but by the will of God they were delivered from the beasts, then they were beheaded, and so passed away to heaven.
<h>I</h>n Auvergne, (in the fifth century,) the holy Confessor Rusticus, Bishop (of Clermont.)
<h>I</h>n the country of Beauvais, (in the seventh century,) holy Geremar, Abbot (of Flay, now called after him Saint-Germer.)
<h>A</h>t San Severino, in the March of Ancona, (in the year 1721) the holy Confessor Pacificus, of the Order of Franciscan Friars Minor of the Reformed Observance, a man of wonderful long-suffering and famous for his love of being alone, whose name Pope Gregory XVI enrolled in the list of the saints.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>M</c>ercifully grant, O Lord, that thine effectual goodness may in all things direct our hearts, forasmuch as without thee we are not able to please thee.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
